blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A tool wants a person's confirmation, but the calling client declared only roots. What must the server avoid?

options.text: Returning a normal result saying it could not ask
options.says: Ruled out because the rule bars only an undeclared request, and the practice's server meets this case with a result "that says the client cannot be asked".

options.text: Sending an elicitation request that the caller never announced
options.says: The first page says "Servers MUST NOT send an inputRequests that the client has not declared support for in its capabilities."

options.text: Ending the call with an error code naming the missing capability
options.says: Ruled out because a server that needs a capability the call did not declare "returns a MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError with code -32021", which is an error code.

options.text: Signing the state of the call so the client cannot alter it
options.says: Ruled out because "servers MUST treat requestState as an attacker-controlled input", so signing it is required, not avoided.

origin.section: What the server owes the state

questions.stem: Two requests carry the same requestState and arrive within its lifetime, one from the user it was issued to and one from a different user. How should the server treat them?

options.text: Reject the second, because the signed payload names its intended principal
options.says: The first page says the state should carry "the authenticated principal, rejecting state presented by a different principal".

options.text: Reject both, since a state may be presented only once
options.says: Ruled out because these measures "do not by themselves guarantee single-use", so the same user can present it again within the lifetime.

options.text: Accept both, because the expiry is the only check the specification requires
options.says: Ruled out because the server also checks "an identifier of the originating request", and the principal.

options.text: Accept both, because a valid signature proves the state is genuine
options.says: Ruled out because the server must reject "rejecting state presented by a different principal" even when the signature is valid.

questions.stem: A load balancer sends consecutive calls of one client to different instances of an MCP server on the 2026-07-28 revision. What does the protocol need so that this works?

options.text: Self-contained requests that carry all their own context
options.says: The first page says the pattern works "without requiring a shared storage layer across server instances or requiring stateful load balancing", and the second page that every POST stands alone.

options.text: A sticky connection that keeps one client on the same instance
options.says: Ruled out because the pattern works "without requiring a shared storage layer across server instances or requiring stateful load balancing".

options.text: A resumable stream that another instance can pick up by its event id
options.says: Ruled out because "Resumable streams through `Last-Event-ID` are not supported."

options.text: A session identifier that each instance looks up in a common table
options.says: Ruled out because MCP in this revision "is stateless and has no protocol-level sessions".

questions.stem: A team plans HTTP-style login for an MCP server that runs as a local child process. What does the specification advise?

options.text: Follow the same flow, since authorization is mandatory for every transport
options.says: Ruled out because "Authorization is OPTIONAL for MCP implementations."

options.text: Use a query-string token, which stdio clients may append to the command
options.says: Ruled out because "Access tokens MUST NOT be included in the URI query string".

options.text: Skip that flow and read credentials from the environment instead
options.says: The second page quotes the specification: "Implementations using an STDIO transport SHOULD NOT follow this specification, and instead retrieve credentials from the environment."

options.text: Ask the user for a password through form-mode elicitation on each start
options.says: Ruled out because "Servers MUST NOT use form mode elicitation to request sensitive information".
